rv.q: The staging is actually too busy, too colorful, too loud, as if Nicholaw doesn't want us to notice that not much of interest is happening.
It’s not shocking that Mean Girls is a fast-paced fancy funtime, but it’s a real treat to find that it’s still witty, worldly, and wise.

That plus the snappy comedy of Fey’s book makes this adaptation of the 2004 movie (which was directed by Mark Waters from a screenplay by Fey) a surprisingly enjoyable and genuinely funny sugar treat with a lot of heart.
But light and frothy though it is, Mean Girls has a kind heart, and there’s always room for another feel-good musical on Broadway.
This is a smart, funny musical that manages to be both true to the film and fresh in its own right.
But who needs Tina Fey to reinvent musical comedy?

Mean Girls succeeds in translating the movie's sharp social commentary into an energetic stage musical.
Fey fans flocking to the show likely will not be disappointed by the often funny but insubstantial stage version
The songs are catchy enough, the book is reasonably witty, the staging sufficiently fluid...But - no offense...'Mean Girls' is basic.
Mean Girls is a solid, entertaining musical that hits its marks without transcending them.
The songs are catchy enough, the dancing is slick and the staging is colorful, but the show as a whole feels oddly inert, lacking the manic energy that made the film so memorable.
The musical version of 'Mean Girls' is more sanitized than satisfying, a Broadway adaptation that feels oddly defanged compared to the sharp-clawed movie that inspired it.
Happily, this time around, a first-class collaboration puts us in the company of "Mean Girls" you will love to hate.
Vibrant, beautifully sung and visually splendid, this funny charmer broadens the original movie to full musical comedy scale without sacrificing any of the mordancy and compassion.
They and the entire company fill every minute of Mean Girls with boundless talent and energy under Casey Nicholaw's fast-paced and imaginative direction and choreography.
Mean Girls is a smart, funny musical that succeeds in translating the beloved movie to the stage while adding its own theatrical magic.

Propelled by dazzling set design and several stand-out performances, the musical — written by Fey, with music by Jeff Richmond, and directed by Casey Nicholaw (The Book of Mormon) — gives fans everything they want while bringing the saga of Regina George and the Plastics into the social media age.
That’s what they’ve achieved here: Mean Girls delightfully fun and funny, silly and sweet, energetic and adorable, sarcastic but good-hearted.
Still, Fey’s baby is a lot of fun.
Mean Girls fans will have a 'fetch' night out at the Broadway musical (see Gretchen, you totally made it happen); they also may wish it was a tad shorter and sharper.

Though Fey has cleverly slipped a dash of new and now into an established crowd-pleasing franchise, Mean Girls is not on the level of truly fresh high school musicals like Hair Spray and Dear Evan Hansen, but more a musical version of what was once classified as B-Movies.
If only Fey’s springboard of a book had inspired more memorable, distinctive songs.

If, like me, you remember being in or around high school in 2004 and aren’t fully convinced that being a teen is any simpler, however more “woke” they may be than we were at that age, then you may find this new take almost too sweet to function.
Tina Fey has brought the musical comedy back to Broadway, and it couldn't have happened at a more necessary time.
Fey’s show has heart, but it’s not terribly fetch.
The effect is to make an already thin, lighthearted story seem painfully threadbare, and to drown out the story's central message about the importance of female unity.
But, as the Girls would put it, this adaptation just isn’t “fetch”.
Despite vibrant performances from a uniformly talented cast, the show drags, especially in the first act.
No, but Broadway may nevertheless welcome its easy, if generic, professionalism.

“Mean Girls,” on the other hand, proves to be a wishy-washy, pointless adaptation of the smart and sassy 2004 film, which was written by Tina Fey and contains performances by Lindsay Lohan, Rachel McAdams, Amanda Seyfried, Lizzy Caplan and Fey.

But as the musical dragged on, I found myself wishing it were weirder, riskier — more willing to try something new rather than phone it in, knowing that audiences will flock no matter how formulaic and lazy an adaptation this is.
Nothing about the musical disappoints...Quite simply, it is a triumph.
Tina Fey’s “Mean Girls” the musical is a triumphant burst of high-energy fun, artfully written and brilliantly executed.
Mean Girls has a bright future on Broadway and I truly cannot say enough good things about it.
Should please both die-hard fans and those looking for a rollicking good time.

"'Mean Girls'—a big, noisy musical based on a hit teen movie...turns out to be one of those feel-good nights on Broadway when you unabashedly jump to your feet applauding because you’ve had such a good time...It comes down to the talent— on the boards to be sure, but more importantly, at the production table...
The set is fantastic, the choreography invigorating, the script impossibly funny and made somehow funnier by the actors' impeccable deliveries.
Tina Fey offers us a new model for musicals about women and girls, one we very sorely needed, with as many big laughs and as much effortless charm as ever.
While many movies have not been improved by being turned into Broadway or Off Broadway musicals, Mean Girls is not only better than the film but it is also vastly entertaining.
Allaying any such concerns, act two has its own twists and turns, ultimately delivering an immensely satisfying conclusion.
It’s full of infectious music, necessary updates, and will remind you why you’re so glad high school is over.
This show has it all: humor, fun, dance, and engagement with the audience.
In conclusion, the show has bounce and verve, it’s joyful and has a healing message; it’s colorful and a delight.
This is a show where you do go out singing the book scenes, but not in a bad way – it's just as entertaining and smart as the film.

While I’m not the target audience for ‘Mean Girls’- in fact, I was surprised the audience was even 35-40% male when I saw it- I appreciate all the ways ‘Mean Girls’ succeeds: it’s funny, touching and emotionally resonant.

Mean Girls -- the musical adaptation of Tina Fey’s hit 2004 film about high school cliques, bullying, and the competitive nature of female friendships -- has arrived on Broadway, and this version will definitely please fans of the original.

Irregardless, to borrow a phrase from Gretchen Weiners, Mean Girls on Broadway is a thrilling cautionary tale, bubbly and full of bite.

Even if it is unlikely that anyone will be humming tunes from Mean Girls, this production proves again that the Broadway musical is an excellent medium for the adaptation of a certain type of film—tongue-in-cheek, youthful, a little sweet, a little sharp, and legitimately funny.
Even a skeptic glad to be far removed from the doings depicted can admire the cast and the staging alive with Broadway expertise.
Colorful, big, exciting and highly entertaining...An entertaining cliché, but a cliché nonetheless.

"That rare movie-to-stage translation that succeeds at almost every level, from its whip-smart writing and frenetically paced scene changes to its timely #MeToo-era message...I can see 'Mean Girls' becoming one of the more enduring movie-inspired musicals to come along in a while.

While Mean Girls should enjoy a healthy Broadway run, it's also exciting to anticipate future high school productions of the show, providing many interesting roles for girls and conveying important messages about accepting others and accepting yourself.
Although the cast is brilliant and vocally astounding the depth of their characters sometimes suffer from stereotype and incessant jokes that jeopardize authenticity.

As Janis might have said, I really wanted this show to be "tits," but it is mostly a bust.
